items.title: Von der Leyen's coalition fractures over need for AI liability rules
items.excerpt: The European Parliament held a heated debate over how to handle AI, with the center-right doubling down on simplification to boost European business while other groups in von der Leyen's coalition pressed for AI liability rules.

history_match.title: Von der Leyen pitches AI as solution to reduce reporting for European businesses

items.title: Socialists push for EU law on deepfakes
items.excerpt: Who owns your face and voice when AI can copy both? The Socialists and Democrats group is pushing for new EU safeguards against deepfakes, though the legal answer is far from simple.

items.title: OpenAI, Anthropic, and Nvidia had record lobbying quarters
items.excerpt: Third-quarter federal lobbying disclosures show OpenAI, Anthropic and Nvidia each set company spending records; Apple also had a record quarter.

items.title: Meta drops the word "train" from its commercial TOS after AI backlash
items.excerpt: Meta revised the commercial terms that publishers said would license AI scraping of their sites, removing the word 'train' but declining to add language respecting robots.txt. (Follow-up to the 10-22 publishers-vs-Meta card; not a pause of the terms.)

history_match.title: Publishers want Brussels and London to stop Meta's new AI terms

items.title: State Department orders 'super intelligence' wording across all official communications
items.excerpt: An internal State Department cable extends the administration's 'super intelligence' terminology change to emails, speeches, websites and official titles, while preserving legal language and historical records.

history_match.title: Inaugurating The Era Of Super Intelligence

items.title: USPTO looks to AI agents to ease examiner workloads
items.excerpt: The U.S. Patent and Trademark Office's acting patents commissioner said putting AI agents in examiners' hands could shorten patent review to about a year.

items.title: Investment summit: German government strikes AI deal with Nvidia
items.excerpt: At the 'Invest in Germany' summit in Berlin, the federal government secured an AI partnership with Nvidia and new Amazon investment, part of Europe's sovereign-compute push.

items.title: Palantir vows NATO AI system has no 'kill switch' after Starlink row
items.excerpt: Palantir says it cannot shut off NATO's AI systems, responding to European fears of dependence on U.S. tech after disruptions to Ukraine's Starshield access.

items.title: Pay locals to love AI? Trump wants data centres to share a 'dividend'
items.excerpt: President Trump urged AI companies on Truth Social to strike 'dividend' deals with local communities to make data-centre developments more popular. (Datacenter angle - plan says avoid a second datacenter card.)

items.title: Age Checks, AI Regulation and Censorship Put Internet Freedom Under Pressure
items.excerpt: Freedom House's latest Freedom on the Net report finds the global fight for internet freedom getting harder, pointing to age checks, AI regulation and censorship.

items.title: European Parliament Divided on How to Govern AI At Home and Abroad
items.excerpt: MEPs back global AI cooperation but disagree on regulation, safeguards and Europe's role in setting the rules. (Likely the same plenary debate as the POLITICO Europe liability item - treat as one story.)

items.title: Who, If Anyone, Should Have a License to Kill AI?
items.excerpt: Lawmakers want AI kill switches, but who pulls the trigger, what it shuts off and when it is justified remain dangerously unclear. (Analysis essay.)

items.title: Beyond the U.S.-China Binary: The New Landscape of AI Partnerships in the Global South
items.excerpt: Global South countries are gaining new choices for AI ecosystems as China, India and the Gulf states expand technology offerings, creating new challenges for U.S. leadership. (Analysis.)

items.title: Ukraine's strikes on Russian data centers disrupt key services and derail AI research
items.excerpt: Ukrainian drones this month hit three Yandex data centers plus Sberbank and VKontakte facilities, disrupting cloud services, Yandex's Alisa assistant and AI chatbots and setting back Russia's AI ambitions. (Verified via MSN syndication AA2fOFiO; apnews.com blocks fetch.)

history_match.title: Ukraine's drones knock out AI data center belonging to "Russia's Google"

items.title: MOFCOM's New Rules and the Future of Chinese AI
items.excerpt: ChinaTalk analyzes China's Commerce Ministry draft export-control rules on AI models and chip designs. (Analysis follow-up to the already-published China export-control draft story.)

history_match.title: China proposes export controls on its advanced AI models and chip designs

items.title: IOPC investigating officer's use of AI in criminal investigations
items.excerpt: The UK police watchdog opened a gross-misconduct investigation into a Derbyshire detective alleged to have used AI to make policy decisions, assess risk and justify decisions, and to have entered sensitive case data into it. (Primary release.)

items.title: Nunes Marques suspende postagens ilegais contra campanha de Lula
items.excerpt: TSE President Nunes Marques ordered removal of about 20 posts by lawmakers allied with Flávio Bolsonaro that the Lula campaign said contained deepfakes, days before Brazil's Oct 25 runoff. (Off-list: no allowed outlet covered the TSE ruling.)

history_match.title: TSE determines that Meta treat Lula and Flávio campaigns equally under fine of R$500 thousand

items.title: Meta descumpre ordens do TSE sobre IA e pode ser multada no Brasil
items.excerpt: Brazil's electoral prosecutor asked the TSE to fine Meta R$1 million per day for failing to comply with orders on its AI tools' treatment of candidates. (Off-list; a request, not yet a TSE ruling - follow-up to the 10-16 Meta AI complaint.)

history_match.title: TSE determines that Meta treat Lula and Flávio campaigns equally under fine of R$500 thousand

items.title: FTC to collect public opinion on draft guidelines against 'AI washing'
items.excerpt: Korea's Fair Trade Commission opened public comment on draft guidelines against ads that exaggerate products' use of AI, so-called AI washing. (Off-list: no allowed outlet carried this Korean regulator action.)

items.title: Mandatory disclosure of AI training data from government-backed projects raises questions over detailed criteria
items.excerpt: South Korea will require AI training data built in government-backed projects to be provided through the national AI Hub from April, and debate is growing over detailed criteria as rules are drafted. (Off-list.)

items.title: Pentagon office for AI oversight is understaffed, government watchdog finds
items.excerpt: A GAO report finds the Pentagon's Chief Digital and AI Office is significantly understaffed, hindering full implementation of its Responsible AI framework. (Off-list; primary is a GAO report.)
